items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)
items.label: Bongo Joe

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是圣多美和普林西比1970至80年代音乐的再发掘，收录15首曲目，呈现当地独特的Puxa风格。Puxa融合了前葡萄牙非洲殖民地音乐元素，与merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等节奏交织，并因葡萄牙曾禁止其舞蹈而具有反抗意味。合辑展现了多重吉他交织、人声与旋律框架互动、节奏层叠的特点，乐队Pedro Lima的吉他即兴与鼓组对峙令人印象深刻。音乐虽然以舞蹈为核心，但复杂的节奏构造和多层器乐编排超越了单纯的舞曲逻辑。发行厂牌Bongo Joe为独立小厂。

items._cn_summary: 这张作品由David Dzubinski作曲，作为Prism Quartet「Unlocking Your Inner Composer」系列合作项目的一部分，于2025年11月在费城免费图书馆首演。演出邀请了人声Ursula Rucker、打击乐Tyshawn Sorey与小提琴Carlos Santiago共同参与编排与演绎。作品在不到四分钟内完成了从粗粝到抒情的情绪转换，展现出精细的处理与充沛的能量。作为弦乐四重奏与自由即兴打击乐、说唱人声的合作，作品融合了当代古典写作与即兴爵士元素，风格跨越多个领域。但乐评本身内容较为简短，更像是一段推荐导言而非深入分析，信息量有限，难以全面判断其艺术深度与创新程度。整体而言，这是面向先锋与小众听众的跨界实验作品，适合对当代即兴与新音乐合作模式感兴趣的听众关注。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民间音乐界经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔，共收录五首曲目，以传统音乐为主，融合了成员各自的音乐视角。整张作品弥漫着古老而略带粗粝的氛围，器乐配置丰富多样：口琴与风笛为作品提供强劲的推进力，扬琴则营造出细腻的背景层次。Guldhammer的嗓音富有说服力与感染力，在器乐曲目中，口琴、笛子与弦乐交织出令人兴奋的失衡感。作为一张出道作品，它展现了该乐队远超初出茅庐水准的成熟度与完成度，五首曲目虽短，却已为听众勾勒出颇具潜力的音乐轮廓。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威乐手组成三重奏，重新诠释斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材。乐评将其比作室内乐般的亲密对话，而非适合舞蹈伴奏的常规演奏，强调对音乐潜在意义与暗流的挖掘。编排上以recorder（文中提到的sjøfløyte）为主奏旋律线，小提琴提供纹理质感伴奏，鼓手则以细腻点缀介入，三件乐器在传统曲调基础上进行解构与重组。以挪威Setesdal山谷的"Fossgrimen"开篇，呼应民间传说中水妖与魔鬼提琴的意象，暗示表层欢快之下的不安因素。在瑞典Polska曲中，引入主题后随即碎裂并戛然而止，展现对传统形式的实验性处理。整体呈现学院派视角下的北欧民间音乐再创造，介于传统与现代之间。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary sound art
items._cn_summary: 这张作品并非传统音乐唱片，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述集。二十五位年龄从十七岁到六十七岁的参与者包括枪击受害者和施害者，录音在一位九十四岁祖母家的前廊完成，当天恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥。编辑明确指出没有添加任何音乐，仅保留环境声与即兴说唱元素。一位老年女性在讲述失去两个儿子的经历时情绪崩溃，反复道歉，而评论认为真正应道歉的是造成统计性不公的社会结构。收益将捐赠给反暴力组织Cure Violence Global。作品以田野录音与口述档案的形式呈现社会现实，与实验音乐和声音艺术有交集，但核心内容是社会纪实而非音乐创作。

items._cn_summary: 这篇文章介绍的是加布里埃尔·博拉尼奥斯创作的打击乐作品《Strobe》的视频首播，由Crossing 32nd Street Ensemble的四位打击乐手演绎。演出中，乐手通过各自的开关盒控制灯光与电子设备，营造出嗡鸣环绕的氛围声场，点状的节奏在电子音效中不时浮现。作品融合了打击乐的物理性与电子媒介的实时控制，色彩丰富的灯光与节拍交替闪烁形成视觉与听觉的双重体验。文本本身更像是一段新闻导语性质的预告，侧重于演出场景的描写而非深入的乐评分析，信息量有限，因此只能作为初步了解的窗口。整体来看，这是一件跨界当代音乐与电子实验的现场作品，适合对当代古典与实验音乐交叉领域感兴趣的听众进一步探索。

items._cn_summary: 本文来自Touching Extremes近期发布的两张实验音乐专辑短评合集。Eamon Sprod的《Foil Void Join Avoid》由Aposiopèse厂牌发行，将四年来在被忽视的室内空间与城市基础设施中采集的声音素材，整合为两套声学音乐（acousmatic）组曲，呈现出对环境声源与空间回响的细致观察。Robert Piotrowicz的《Wrong Filament》由Merkurial厂牌发行，以合成器为载体，融合非对称节拍、微分音变化以及想象中的东欧舞蹈传统，六首电子作品在具象与抽象之间游走。两张专辑均属于独立/小众发行，面向实验音乐深度听众。文章本身为评测合辑性质的转载，内容较为简短，缺少对作品具体声音质地与艺术意图的深入分析，但所涉及的音乐方向与实验/前卫、电子领域高度契合。

items.body: The album was originally released during the formative years of Kompakt's long-running Pop Ambient series Photo by David Westlake Markus Guentner's ambient and dub techno classic LP In Moll is being reissued to mark its 25th anniversary. The record has been newly remastered by composer and mastering engineer Rafael Anton Irisarri for its new edition. Speaking about the record, Irisarri said: "It immediately opened a door to a world of music I didn't know existed. Markus showed me entirely new possibilities for what electronic music could communicate." The updated release takes in fresh visual elements created by Guentner himself as he revisited the album 25 years on, while the track 'In Moll 4' will appear on vinyl for the first time as part of... The post Markus Guentner’s ‘In Moll’ Set for 25th Anniversary Reissue appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Markus Guentner的《In Moll》发行于Kompakt厂牌Pop Ambient系列形成初期，是融合氛围与dub techno的经典专辑。此次25周年再版由母带工程师Rafael Anton Irisarri重新处理音质，Irisarri本人表示该专辑曾为他打开电子音乐表达可能性的全新视野。再版还包含Guentner本人重新创作的视觉元素，并首次以黑胶形式收录曲目'In Moll 4'。该作在欧洲电子场景中具有标杆地位，为后续氛围电子与极简律动的发展铺设了路径，重新发行让新一代听众有机会接触这部里程碑作品。

items.body: Jeremy Allen speaks to the recently reinvigorated experimental synth pop band about covering an entire album by The Fall and the changing scene for electronic music Globo have never really fitted in. That was certainly true when the renegade cell of electronically-minded musicians released their debut album Pro War in 1995, armed with just Akai samplers, drum machines and their wits. items._cn_summary: 本文为The Quietus对英国实验合成器流行乐队Globo的采访报道。乐队1993年在诺里奇成立，首张专辑《Pro War》于1995年发行，仅凭Akai采样器、鼓机和个人直觉创作。他们曾被拿来与Underworld比较，但与当时伦敦为中心的Britpop浪潮格格不入。乐队核心成员包括记者出身的Mark Wernham、插画师Steve Appleton和电影制作人Paul Thompson。本文主要围绕乐队翻唱The Fall整张专辑的计划展开，并探讨电子音乐场景的变迁。作为一篇人物访谈而非深度乐评，内容偏向背景介绍与乐队动态，对音乐本身的分析有限。

items._cn_summary: Andrea Orlando是意大利摇滚乐场景中的鼓手，曾参与La Coscienza Di Cena、Finisterre及Höstsonaten等多个乐队，深植于热那亚的Zuffanti音乐圈。《La Scienza delle Stagioni》是其第二张个人专辑，邀请了该圈内的多位乐手合作，包括Zuffanti本人、Finisterre的Boris Valle、La Coscienza di Zeno的Luca Scherani等。专辑延续了意大利前卫摇滚的传统路线，以鼓手和键盘为核心，融入了mellotron、organ、moog等经典RPI音色元素，吉他部分由Marcella Arganese、Laura Marsano（两位女性乐手）或Stefano Mareelli担任。整体制作偏向复古的意大利交响前卫风格，与实验、爵士或电子领域几乎无交集，是该特定小圈子内的延续性作品。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — The Roaring Waves by Hackett & Rothery sees 2 prog rock guitar legends coming together to create a very enjoyable if slightly tedious instrumental album. No one can take away the impact Steve Hackett & Steve Rothery have on the progressive rock world, with early Genesis & Marillion being a massive influence on the entire modern prog scene since the 70s & 80s, and their monumental playing is always an ace card. But while they bring such talent to these bands, they are the type of guitarists who contribute to a group more than themselves as solo instrumentalists. But the noticeable styles between the 2 are noticeable and they do compliment each other well. The tracks are very well composed and performed, but there isn't too much meat on the bone. It is overall very well mixed too. I'd give this a high 6 to low 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is The Roaring Waves.
items._cn_summary: 《The Roaring Waves》是Steve Hackett与Steve Rothery两位前卫摇滚吉他传奇人物的合作专辑，以纯器乐形式呈现。两位吉他手各自以早期Genesis与Marillion的身份对现代前卫摇滚场景产生了深远影响，他们的演奏技巧在这张专辑中得到充分展现。整体编排严谨、混音精良，两人的演奏风格差异明显但相互补足，形成良好的对话感。然而专辑在内容深度上略显单薄，曲目虽精心打造却缺乏足够的实质支撑，呈现出"好听但稍显冗长"的特质。作为一张面向前卫摇滚爱好器的吉他演奏专辑，它在技艺层面值得肯定，但在突破性与实验性上并无太多建树，适合喜欢经典前卫吉他演奏的听众聆听。

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 987"The Roaring Waves" is a collaborative album by two influential names in the European prog scene, Steve Hackett and Steve Rothery. As we know, Hackett was the main guitarist of Genesis and Rothery is the guitarist of Marillion. As we also know, Marillion was the band most close to Genesis of all British prog bands that appeared in the 80's. So, we can say that Rothery is, somehow, the heir of Hackett on guitars. So, we can not be surprised by this collaborative effort.Although the initial idea emerged around 2015, "The Roaring Waves" took nearly a decade to be written and recorded. The sessions were split between the Racket Club (Marillion's studio) and the home studios of both musicians. The strong connection between both solidified on stage when Rothery joined Hackett at the Royal Albert Hall in 2024 to play "Fly On A Windshield", one of the most famous tracks of the album "The Lamb Lies Down On Broadway" by Genesis.So, "The Roaring Waves" is the first instrumental collaborative project between two of the most iconic guitarists in progressive rock. The album is a profoundly cinematic, atmospheric and a melodic work, entirely inspired by the power, mysteries and nuances of the sea, beautifully paced conversation between two master guitarists. Instead of a flashy "speed trial" or shred-fest competition, the album prioritizes compositional patience, atmospheric depth, and melodic trade-offs. Hackett's angular, classical-tinged and experimental approach, merges seamlessly with Rothery's emotional soaring sustain. Having decided to completely forgo vocals and lyrics, the album gives the listener a true complete imaginative freedom through textures that blend progressive rock, classical music, ambient and electronic textures.The line up on "The Roaring Waves" is Steve Hackett (guitar and harmonica) and Steve Rothery (guitar, bass guitar and keyboards). "The Roaring Waves" also had the participation of Riccardo Romano (keyboards and bass guitar), Daniele Pomo and Leon Parr (drums)."The Storm" is the dramatic opening of the album. It begins by placing the listener in the midst of a storm, with the guitars intertwining to create the tension and force of a storm at sea. This is a beautiful, wild and cinematic piece that delights the listener, a track that serves more as an introduction to the album than in a particularly loud announcement. "Sandsend" is a more restful and contemplative track, where the tension eases, evoking a sense of isolation, a cool beauty and serene atmospheres. It veers a measured rhythm, toward elegant and melancholic atmospheres reminiscent of Pink Floyd, letting the guitars literally sing in unison. At under five minutes, the track is correspondingly compact. "Red Dragon" is the shortest track on the album where Hackett introduces the sitar guitar to give the composition a mystical and an oriental sound. It brings a touch of world music to the otherwise rather watertight soundscape with folkloric influences, bagpipes and sitar sounds. This is a more playful and less polished piece than its predecessors. The title track "The Roaring Waves" is probably the most compelling moment on the album. It begins with a beautiful flourish of classical guitar by Hackett. It's one of the album's highlights, the real swell. Slowly, the swelling dynamics, guitars giving each other space, and precisely that blend of melancholy and pathos for both Steves, a real classic prog moment. "K-129" is one of the most experimental and intriguing tracks on the album. Electronic soundscapes and dark guitars create a very own feeling. Once again, this rhythmic framework is layered over the two guitarists in a largely improvisational style. It stands out paying homage to the "Kosmische Musik" and the Berlin School of the 70's. It reminds me of "Gento", by Bisocope of last year, the project of Rothery and Thorsten Quaeschning of Tangerine Dream. For me, it's one of the strongest tracks on the album. "The Black Sea", described by the authors as a dark adventure, was chosen as the lead single of the album. It's one of the album's great melancholic beauties. Rothery's warm guitar meets Hackett's finely crafted timbres. This is precisely where it becomes clear why this collaboration makes any sense at all. "Pacific Coast Highway" departs from the gray and icy atmosphere of the previous tracks, an unexpected track. Here, the music gains rhythm and movement with Hackett playing harmonica and slide guitar, evoking a high-speed car trip along the sunny California coast. It's a lighthearted, road-movie-esque jam with plenty of vocals at the end of it.Conclusion: "The Roaring Waves" is a dialogue between two musicians who respect and listen to each other, and who have acquired the wisdom of guitarists who have nothing left to prove. It's, therefore, a mature, profound and extremely refined work. "The Roaring Waves" remains above all an album on which two guitarists thankfully dedicate themselves not to themselves, but to the respective piece and its shared concept. Hackett and Rothery harmonize superbly with each other, instead of getting lost in an endless competition for the more spectacular solo. Compared with the album "GTR" of Hackettt and Howe, this is a much better work. I know, those were the 80's. But I don't know if it's an excuse.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是前Genesis吉他手Steve Hackett与Marillion吉他手Steve Rothery的首张器乐合作专辑，历时近十年完成。整张作品以海洋为灵感主题，呈现电影化、氛围化的吉他对话。两位吉他手摒弃人声，以旋律互换和纹理编织为核心手段：Hackett带来棱角分明、古典倾向的实验性手法，Rothery则以情感充沛的延音与之交织。作品融合前卫摇滚、古典、氛围与电子音效，开篇《The Storm》用交织的吉他营造海上风暴的张力，《Sandsend》呈现宁静沉思的氛围，《Red Dragon》引入西塔吉他增添东方色彩和世界音乐元素。整体偏向旋律驱动和氛围营造，而非炫技式速弹。

items.body: Catherine Ringer, vocalist, songwriter, and co-founder of French new wave duo Les Rita Mitsouko, has died at age 68. Her children announced her death in a statement to AFP, confirming that she died from cancer on the night of September 14, 2026. With her partner in music and life, Fred Chichin, Ringer made pop music feel large enough to accommodate almost anything: punk impatience, funk, cabaret, electronic experimentation, and the expressive possibilities of French chanson. A song could be funny, sensual, disconcerting, and profoundly sad within the same few minutes. Ringer gave each feeling its own physical presence, singing with a freedom that made conventional ideas of good taste seem rather timid. Born on October 18, 1957, in Suresnes, near Paris, she was the daughter of painter Sam Ringer, a Polish-born Jewish Holocaust survivor, and an architect mother. She left school at 15 and pursued an artistic education through theatre, music, and dance. Among the formative figures in her life was Argentine dancer and choreographer Marcia Moretto, who became her teacher and collaborator. Those years onstage helped establish the connection between movement and voice that would distinguish her work with Les Rita Mitsouko. Nostalgie’s biography documents her early performances and work with Moretto. Ringer met Chichin in 1979, beginning a partnership that would carry them from the Paris underground to international recognition. Their self-titled 1984 debut, recorded with Conny Plank, introduced a group whose appetite for experiment came with a formidable instinct for melody. As Coilhouse’s retrospective observed, Ringer’s background in avant-garde theatre remained visible in the duo’s performances and videos. Marcia Baïla became their breakthrough. Written in remembrance of Moretto following her death from cancer, it joined the exhilaration of dance to the shock of losing someone whose life had been devoted to movement. Its popularity carried that private grief into public celebration. The song offers an especially poignant way to remember Ringer now: affection, anger, and delight sharing the same space, with no easy separation between them. Directed by Philippe Gautier, the music video for Marcia Baïla gave the song an equally extravagant visual life, with costumes by Jean Paul Gaultier and Thierry Mugler. Watch the video below. The duo’s collaboration with Tony Visconti on The No Comprendo in 1986 brought Andy, C’est comme ça, and Les Histoires d’A. The album won at the 1987 Victoires de la Musique, as did Jean-Baptiste Mondino’s video for C’est comme ça. These songs remain an excellent introduction to Ringer’s range: the teasing insistence of Andy, the sharp attack of C’est comme ça, and the ease with which she could make a repeated phrase feel like an argument, an invitation, or a joke. Their creative world extended well beyond records. Jean-Luc Godard included the duo at work in his 1987 film Soigne ta droite, while collaborations brought them together with fellow musical eccentrics. Sparks joined them for Singing in the Shower, from 1988’s Marc & Robert, a meeting of artists who understood how much pleasure could be found in pop’s peculiar corners. Later, Iggy Pop appeared on My Love Is Bad, preserved alongside their other collaborations in the band’s collected catalogue. The apparent playfulness could also carry terrible knowledge. Le Petit Train addressed the deportation trains of the Holocaust, a history bound closely to her father’s survival. Its video, filmed in Bombay, placed Ringer amid exuberant dancing while the words described people being carried toward their deaths. The tension between the music’s invitation and the lyric’s meaning remains deeply unsettling. She understood how a familiar pleasure could open an audience to something painful. Chichin died from cancer in 2007, aged 53, the year Les Rita Mitsouko released Variéty. Ringer continued performing their songs while building a solo catalogue that included Ring n’ Roll in 2011 and Chroniques et fantaisies in 2017. With Plaza Francia, alongside Gotan Project’s Eduardo Makaroff and Christoph H. Müller, she explored tango on 2014’s A New Tango Song Book. Her later work also returned to the intimacy of spoken language. In L’Érotisme de vivre, she performed the poetry of Alice Mendelson, accompanied by pianist Grégoire Hetzel under the direction of Mauro Gioia. The scale had changed, but the curiosity remained: another writer, another setting, another way to give words a body. Ringer leaves music full of appetite and contradiction, open to beauty without becoming polite about it. She made eccentricity feel generous, something an audience could participate in. Our thoughts are with her family, friends, collaborators, and everyone who found freedom in her voice. Follow Catherine Ringer: Instagram Facebook Follow Les Rita Mitsouko Instagram YouTube Bandcamp The post Catherine Ringer, the Extraordinary Voice of Les Rita Mitsouko, Has Passed Away at 68 appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items._cn_summary: 这篇悼念文章追溯了法国新浪潮双人组合Les Rita Mitsouko主唱Catherine Ringer的艺术生涯。她与音乐及人生搭档Fred Chichin合作，将朋克的躁动、放克的律动、卡巴莱的戏剧感、电子实验与法国香颂融为一体，使流行音乐具备了容纳几乎一切元素的张力。从与德国制作人Conny Plank合作的首张专辑，到Tony Visconti制作的第二张专辑，贯穿始终的是旋律直觉与实验欲望的并存。为纪念已故编舞家Marcia Moretto而作的Marcia Baïla将舞蹈的欢愉与丧失亲人的震动合而为一，至今仍是理解其艺术核心的最佳入口。文章同时追溯了她在戏剧与舞蹈方面的训练背景如何塑造了舞台表现力，并提及与Jean-Luc Godard、Jean Paul Gaultier、Thierry Mugler等艺术家的跨界合作。整体内容偏重生平叙述与音乐史回顾，并非深度乐评。

items.body: Synthpop project TéMèT releases the single “What We Are” on 2 October 2026 on all platforms. The track leans into a Depeche Mode-inspired synthpop sound, more melodic and atmospheric than the project’s previous, darker and more energetic releases. Lyrically, “What We Are” traces a slow unraveling, something rising to the surface that can no longer be hidden, building toward the refrain: “We become what we are.” TéMèT has previously been featured by Side-Line and EBM.gr, and the track “Discord” was included in eLxAr’s Retro Music August compilation. About TéMèT TéMèT is a synthpop and darkwave duo, K1 and MYK, based in Strasbourg, France. The project’s name draws on Tem, the ancient Egyptian deity associated with the setting sun and with creation and endings, and its sound mixes a melodic, atmospheric register influenced by acts such as Depeche Mode with the darker, more energetic material in its earlier catalogue. The duo’s single “Discord,” described by its members as sitting between Depeche Mode and OMD, was released in August 2026, covered by Side-Line and EBM.gr, and later included in eLxAr’s Retro Music August compilation. “What We Are” follows as TéMèT’s next single, out 2 October 2026 on all platforms.
items._cn_summary: 法国斯特拉斯堡双人组TéMèT即将发行新单曲《What We Are》，延续其一贯的合成器流行路线。这首作品在风格上更偏向Depeche Mode式的旋律化与氛围化处理，相较于此前更暗、更具能量感的老作品有所调整。歌词围绕某种逐渐显露、无法再隐藏的事物展开，最终汇聚于'我们成为我们所是'这一副歌主题。项目名取自古埃及日落之神Tem，音乐融合了Depeche Mode式的氛围旋律与早期作品中更黑暗、更具攻击性的元素。此前发行的单曲《Discord》曾被Side-Line与EBM.gr报道，并入选eLxAr八月合辑。整体而言，这是一篇新单曲发布的新闻通告，描述清晰但缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论与听感分析。

items.body: California duo Antania release the single and video “33”, the first taste of their new album The Unholy 33, due 16 October 2026 via Argonauta Records. The digital album follows, with physical CD and vinyl editions to be detailed later. Antania, the project of Doc Luna and Kali Mortem, build “33” entirely without conventional guitars or bass, relying instead on synthesizers, distorted textures and machine-like rhythms. The duo describe their sound as avant-garde black metal filtered through industrial and experimental electronics, citing Dødheimsgard, Mysticum and Thorns alongside the dark electronic legacies of Skinny Puppy and Ministry as reference points. “The Unholy 33” runs eleven tracks: “33”, “DVHM3R”, “Sn0wAnGeL”, “Gloomzday”, “ThUgG33”, “Cykl0pZ”, “Flies”, “AntVniV”, “Frazzledrip”, “Kultz” and “HEarSe”. Following the album’s release, Doc Luna and Kali Mortem head to Asia in support, joining Swedish extreme metal act The Crown for dates in the UAE, Japan and South Korea, followed by an appearance alongside Evergrey in India. About Antania Antania is the Californian duo of Doc Luna and Kali Mortem. The project began as a doom-bass act, releasing the debut album “Lividity” in 2023 before signing with Triad Records later that year. Antania supported Psyclon Nine on a 2024 European tour alongside Devil M. “The Unholy 33” marks the duo’s move to Argonauta Records and a shift toward the avant-garde industrial black metal sound built entirely from electronics.
items._cn_summary: 加州二人组 Antania 即将发行的专辑《The Unholy 33》以全电子化手段构建前卫黑金属，摒弃传统吉他和贝斯，依靠合成器、失真质感和机械节拍堆叠声音。从doom-bass出发的两人此次转向更为极端的实验方向，参考Dødheimsgard、Mysticum、Thorns等北欧黑金属传统，同时融入Skinny Puppy和Ministry式的暗电子血脉。专辑收录十一首曲目，曲名如DVHM3r、Sn0wAnGeL、Cykl0pZ等以数字与字母混合命名，暗示数字时代密码式的美学取向。Argonauta Records作为独立厂牌发行，配合亚洲巡演计划，显示出地下场景的活跃度。全电子黑金属的概念虽然有趣，但与北欧前辈相比，原创辨识度尚需作品实际呈现来验证。

items.body: Swedish goth pioneers The Bizarre Orkeztra have reissued “Land” as a 2026 remaster, out now through COMEDIA in collaboration with Ambush Records. The track is the first release in a new series of remastered singles drawn from the band’s catalog. “Land” was written by Sonny Jansson and originally released in 1984 as a 12″ single on Ambush Records, the band’s own indie label. The original tracklist, “Land,” “Korridor,” “Justice” and “Travelling Man,” was recorded by Christer Björklund at The Bizarre Orkeztra’s headquarters, with vocals recorded by Jomma Sundström at Gävle Ljudstudio and production by Bob Boxkopf. Copies of the 12″ came with an eight-page comic booklet, “The No! COMIX No.2,” made specifically for the release. For the 2026 edition, the title track has been remastered by Håkan Nilsson, with Richard Solstjärna serving as executive producer and providing the new cover art. The single is available digitally, including on Spotify, with a release date of 16 September 2026. COMEDIA describes the campaign as presenting “carefully selected highlights drawn from the band’s impressive back catalog.” It is not the first time “Land” has reached digital platforms: the track was previously issued as a remastered digital reissue in 2020, at the time as part of a monthly reissue project with a companion schedule that also covered “Visions On The Wall,” “Midnight Show,” “A Beautiful Place,” “Hunger For Pleasure” and “She’s Got.” The 2026 edition relaunches that catalog campaign as a new series of remastered singles. About The Bizarre Orkeztra The Bizarre Orkeztra formed in Gävle, Sweden, in the early 1980s, emerging from the punk rock band PF Commando and the avant-garde post-punk band Modaern Art. The band was among the first goth acts in Sweden. Its original lineup was Sonny Jansson on vocals and guitars, Richard Sandberg on drums and guitar, and Ola Claesson on bass and backing vocals; Håkan Nilsson later joined on synthesizer for the group’s later recordings. “Land” was the band’s debut release under The Bizarre Orkeztra name, following the 1981 recording “Ingen kärlek, Inget hat,” released under the group’s earlier name, Bizarre Sex. Two studio albums followed on Ambush Records: “Visions On The Wall” in 1985 and “A Beautiful Place” in 1987, along with the singles “Midnight Show” in 1986 and “She’s Got” in 1989. The album “Hunger For Pleasures,” released in 1988, featured Joakim Lindgren on saxophone alongside Nilsson’s synthesizer work. The band released three albums and several singles in total before disbanding in the late 1980s. Bass player Ola “Toli” Claesson, who died in 2009, created cover art for several of the band’s albums and singles, including the comic strip made for “Land,” which was handed out to the audience at the band’s first concert in Gävle. COMEDIA’s new remastered singles series revisits that catalog, beginning again with the track that first introduced The Bizarre Orkeztra to record buyers in 1984.
items._cn_summary: The Bizarre Orkeztra 作为瑞典早期哥特/后朋克先驱之一，将1984年首张单曲《Land》以2026年新版重制发行，由COMEDIA与乐队自有厂牌Ambush Records合作推出。新版本由Håkan Nilsson负责重制母带，Richard Solstjärna担任执行制作并设计全新封面，数字平台同步上线。乐队从PF Commando和Modaern Art等朋克与前卫后朋克组合演变而来，作品融合阴郁氛围与实验倾向，原版12寸唱片还附有八页漫画册。整体来看，这是一次对早期瑞典暗潮场景的重新梳理，文章更偏向资讯性梳理而非深度乐评，但作为该流派的考古材料仍有参考价值。

items._cn_summary: 本文为日本文化厅主办的「MUSIC LOVES ART 2026」项目报道，探讨音乐与美术融合的策展理念。展示作家包括いすたえこ、GOO CHOKI PAR、evala、渡辺明日香等跨领域创作者，其中evala以实验电子与声音艺术闻名，GOO CHOKI PAR以图形设计与装置见长。项目尝试打破音乐会与美术展览的传统边界，让视觉与声音在同一空间对话。然而原文仅为新闻预告性质，内容不足200字符，缺乏对具体作品声音设计、演出形式与艺术语汇的深度评析，难以判断其在实验音乐层面的实际完成度。作为艺术跨界策展的报道具有一定参考价值，但信息密度过低，不足以构成完整的乐评。

items.excerpt: 〈環境破壊と資本主義の終焉〉をテーマに深い海の底――意識の深層へと手を伸ばした5年ぶりの新作。ARAKI Shin、marucoporoporo、Kumi Takaharaをゲストに迎え、当人のフィンガー・ピッキングによるギターに微かなノイズや柔和な管絃楽器の音色を重ねた本作がもたらすのは、有機的なアンビエンスと安らぎにも似た静寂。瞑想的な美しさを纏ったポスト・クラシカル作品だ。
items.body: 〈環境破壊と資本主義の終焉〉をテーマに深い海の底――意識の深層へと手を伸ばした5年ぶりの新作。ARAKI Shin、marucoporoporo、Kumi Takaharaをゲストに迎え、当人のフィンガー・ピッキングによるギターに微かなノイズや柔和な管絃楽器の音色を重ねた本作がもたらすのは、有機的なアンビエンスと安らぎにも似た静寂。瞑想的な美しさを纏ったポスト・クラシカル作品だ。
items._cn_summary: 日本创作人Motohiro Nakashima（中岛元博）相隔五年推出的新专辑《Sea of Thought》，以环境破坏与资本主义终结为思想背景，将意识比作深海，向潜意识的底层探索。作品以他本人的指弹吉他为核心，叠加微妙的噪音层次与柔和的管弦乐音色，营造出有机的氛围声响。客座乐手包括ARAKI Shin、marucoporoporo与Kumi Takahara，他们在编曲中提供了多样化的器乐纹理。整体风格属于冥想式的后古典音乐，旋律克制、音色柔和，介于氛围音乐与现代古典之间，注重情绪的内在沉淀而非戏剧性展开。

items.album: 石川紅奈『Garden』ラテンなオリジナル曲やチック・コリアのカバーも秀逸な初のセルフプロデュース作

items.excerpt: 小曽根真に見出された日本ジャズ界の新星による初のセルフ・プロデュース作品。ウッド・ベースを弾きながら歌う女性と聞くとエスペランサ・スポルディングを思い出すが、よりポップ感覚に溢れ、軽やかで癒しを感じる歌声である。エスペランサのスタイルからの影響もあると語る石川だが、今作ではオリジナル曲も多く、より彼女らしさが出てきた。オリジナルの“Witch of the North”はラテンなリズムの中で伸びやかに跳ね、ロイ・エアーズの“Searching”、チック・コリアの“Time’s Lie”といったカバー曲では70年代ソウルの色を出しつつも柔らかさも感じる石川らしい歌声とアレンジが秀逸だ。

items.body:
V.I.V.E.K Offers More Low-Pressure Dubstep With 'The Escape To Nowhere', The 50th Release On His Label

16 September 2026

As V.I.V.E.K, Vivek Sharda has been one of the most consistent purveyors of unadulterated dubstep, presenting it in the low-pressure form which audibly develops from the Jamaican sound system, dub and reggae culture. The London-based artist has been championed for it over 2 decades by some of the genre's pioneering labels, like his contemporary Mala's imprint Deep Medi Musik, and has flown similar flags through his own party and imprint under the SYSTEM Music umbrella.

Marking the 50th release for his label, Sharda has just released the album 'The Escape To Nowhere', returning to the deep weight and minimal layers of early dubstep after a move towards ambient and IDM influences on his 2024 EP 'Reflections'.

The 8-track release carries its dominating basslines, sometimes over highly syncopated broken beats like on 'The Pattern', other times over more familiar 2-step grooves like on 'Minimal ', and even more organic roots and reggae drumming like on the closer 'Devils Tunnel at 3am'. Over the varied rhythms, Sharda builds his sonic world through echoes of barely-there hooks and vocal samples that dissipate like vapour into the empty ethers he leaves between the layers.

Dandelion, a recurring vocal artist on the label, introduces this dream-like world through his chant-like songwriting on the opener 'Grown'. Later on, airy horns provide similar hypnotising moves on 'Kiss The Sky', a track that V.I.V.E.K also reinterpreted with Rajasthan's Manganiyar musicians during the residency, Fieldlines, at Magnetic Fields Festival 2024.

Check out 'The Escape To Nowhere' below and follow V.I.V.E.K's artist profile for more information.

Image by Shrey Arora for Magnetic Fields Festival 2024

items._cn_summary: V.I.V.E.K 以厂牌 SYSTEM Music 发行第五十张专辑《The Escape To Nowhere》，回归早期 dubstep 的深沉低频与极简层次。八首曲目在节奏上呈现多元面貌：从碎拍切分的《The Pattern》到两步 groove 的《Minimal》，再到收尾曲带有根源雷鬼鼓点的《Devils Tunnel at 3am》。人声采样与回声钩子在层与层的留白中消散，营造出朦胧声场。客座人声 Dandelion 以吟唱式旋律开篇，《Kiss The Sky》中空灵铜管则提供催眠式律动，该曲曾在 2024 年 Magnetic Fields 音乐节驻地项目 Fieldlines 中与拉贾斯坦邦的 Manganiyar 乐手合作重塑，呈现出英式低音音乐与印度传统跨文化对话的一面。

items.body: In this latest instalment of the Secret History of Film Music, Philip Brophy considers how Jon Brion’s music engenders sympathy for the flawed characters in Paul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another (2025) and Punch-Drunk Love (2002), and Greta Gerwig’s Lady Bird (2017). As discussed in the previous essay in this series, Jonny Greenwood provides an amazing score for Paul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another (2025). But two pieces by an earlier composer of Anderson’s films bookend the movie: Jon Brion’s “Bunker Bumper” and “Global Bully”. In One Battle After Another, they function as quietly majestic statements of the drive and exhaustion which propel the intergenerational tale of social reparation and familial separation. “Bunker Bumper” uncoils as a disjointed bossa nova: a gently struck bass drum marks time for the snare, hi-hats and cymbals, skipping with a detached, dainty air. Horns and strings entwine like a billowing flag in slow motion. Sometimes the horns are silenced as the strings climb high, as if they’re searching for something. The music feels absent of harmonic progression; it simply surges, even struggles ahead. It plays near the opening as Pat (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Perfidia (Teyana Taylor) and their radical group French 75 attack a border internment camp. The music intones a sad, fatalistic comment on the limited impact of such revolutionary zeal despite the commitment of its participants. The second track “Global Bully” plays at the film’s end. Years later, Pat relaxes at home with his young adult daughter Willa (Chase Infiniti), offspring of Pat and the long absent Perfidia. The domestic scene shows Willa reading a letter from her mother. In a voiceover, Perfidia acknowledges her mistake in deserting Willa, and expresses hope they will one day meet again. Over a lilting percussive pattern, more strings and horns are orchestrated, but here they coalesce around a chordal pattern. The drums call to mind the tinklers of North American tribal shell shakers engaged in ceremonial dances; the orchestra feels like a calming eulogy played at a church service. The piece acquiesces to how the feisty past can dissolve into a depleted present. It concludes with a touching embrace between Pat and Willa. To label the placement of “Global Bully” here as mere closure misses the weight and precision that Brion’s music bestows on the scene. Across Anderson’s first four films, Brion developed a unique modus operandi of embedding music into movies which, arguably, redefined standard operations of ‘scoring’ and ‘accompaniment’. These two Brion tracks in One Battle After Another were recorded and produced 23 years earlier, for Anderson’s Punch-Drunk Love (2002). That film’s sessions saw Brion continually feeding Anderson with ideas, sketches, recordings and even multitrack breakdowns. All were offered not as thorny strictures, but as flexible flotsam to be experimented with, in terms of how their sono-musical character could enhance and shape onscreen characters. How apt that some of these unused tracks surfaced decades later. As Brion has said: “There are lots of [film composers] doing great things, but it comes down to the director’s ‘follow-through’.” A small suite of prepared piano and percussion ensemble pieces makes up a sizable part of the Punch-Drunk Love score. They sound jittery and clackety, like a wooden digestive system attempting to process parts of a drum kit. They initially read as sound effects more than music – a perceptual doubting, enabled by Gary Rydstrom’s deft mix which folds Brion’s trap kit into Christopher Scarabosio’s sound design (who has handled every Paul Thomas Anderson film since). “Le Petit Chateau” and “Hands And Feet” were based on micro-cassette recordings Brion made of Anderson verbally articulating his ideas for rhythms he wanted to use as timing devices for the film’s long tracking shots. The voice of Anderson became the hands of Brion which became the limbs of Barry (Adam Sandler) who discombobulates throughout the movie in arabesques of anxiety. Upon its release, many assumed the film to be a comedy, thanks to Sandler, but the point was there for an attuned audience: mentally unstable people often appear ‘ridiculous’, but to laugh at their pained performance is inhumane, not to mention imperceptive. Brion’s music plays two roles here. The first, through its percussive moments, is to sonorise the synaptic hell of Barry’s panic attacks, and how desperately out of sync he is with his own body and those around him. The second lies in the sumptuous waltzes (“Punch-Drunk Melody”, “Third Floor Hallway”, “Blossoms & Blood”) which spread the wondrous hope Barry glimpses when he falls in love with Lena (Emily Watson). Irrespective of cliche, the luscious orchestral arrangements welcome the couple into a better, dreamier world. Brion’s music is key in distinguishing Punch-Drunk Love from early 2000s romcom saturation. His arrangements are subtly saccharine, influenced by the lush strings found in rock and pop ballads circa the 1970s, arranged by Van Dyke Parks, Jack Nitzsche and Paul Buckmaster. Their sonority affectionately referenced the easy listening sparkle of 1950/60s hi-fi arrangements by Nelson Riddle and Les Baxter, through to Percy Faith and Paul Mauriat. Brion’s encyclopaedic embrace of recorded popular music is felt in his distinctive melodic sensibility: a transatlantic nexus of solo-Beatles songcraft and Laurel Canyon recording. To be clear, the recording studio rules here, not the concert hall. Punch-Drunk Love used vintage microphones for many of its sessions. The film score brims with detail, space and clarity. Following Punch-Drunk Love, non-mainstream cinema forged a strange meld of nerdy empathy, hipster cynicism and feminist angles in ‘relationship dramedies’: David O Russell’s I Heart Huckabees (2004); Charlie Kaufman’s Eternal Sunshine Of The Spotless Mind (2004) and Synecdoche, New York (2008); Miranda July’s The Future (2011); Judd Apatow’s This Is 40 (2012) and Trainwreck (2015); and Greta Gerwig’s Lady Bird (2017). These films cannily merged po-faced ridicule with heartfelt feeling, to varying degrees of success. Yet in all these titles, Brion’s music fortifies their narratives with an endearing romantic sensibility earned by their dysfunctional, antisocial and ‘spectrum’ characters. His Canyon-esque saunter and rich instrumental layering ameliorates any dismissive urges the films’ characters elicit. In Lady Bird, the titular lead (Saoirse Ronan) feels intentionally unlikeable. Equally deliberate is how Brion’s score waltzes around Lady Bird’s teen sense of independence. The film concludes with Lady Bird finally on her own, enrolled in a New York college. At a public phone, she leaves a message for her mother, admitting the rupturing effects of her teen angst created a wedge between them. Brion performs the resonant piano theme like a silent movie accompanist: trilling high notes and copying what’s happening on screen while allowing it space. Eternal Sunshine Of The Spotless Mind features similar piano themes played over scenes with onscreen dialogue mixed low. This isn’t simply a formal sonic device: it displaces the viewer/auditor from the psychic space of the story – where you identify or read what’s happening to characters on screen – and relocates you within the characters’ headspace. Positioned this way, the audience can feel a touch exposed, implicated in being present when characters are at their most vulnerable. “Global Bully” fades up in One Battle After Another as we see Lockjaw (Sean Penn) gassed and hear Pat prepare Willa for Perfidia’s letter: death and life fused through emotive exhalation. That seems to be a throughline in the work Brion has provided across the film and music industries. In discussions with Anderson, Brion noted the aim of Punch-Drunk Love was to “feel like a musical, but nobody ever breaks into song”. Brion’s music – and his tremulous voice which has appeared in songs in many of the films mentioned – is similarly shaped by repression, tension and elation, in a fountain of emotional surges. Musical theatre sceptics mostly react against the unbridled emotionalism of onscreen characters liberated from their realistic surroundings. Yet this transcendental effect functions perfectly in recorded songs and popular music in general, generating one of music’s prime private pleasures. Brion and his collaborators have long embraced how song sonics skilfully embedded in the production of a film score can be exhilaratingly transgressive. Wire subscribers can read Philip Brophy’s original Secret History of Film Music columns from the 1990s online in the digital archive. It was revived in 2025 as an online column: previous instalments published on The Wire website can be read here. Wire readers and print and digital subscribers can also find this essay on page 16 of The Wire 512.
items._cn_summary: 本文聚焦作曲家Jon Brion为Paul Thomas Anderson电影所作的配乐片段及其跨时空运用。文中以《One Battle After Another》中的两首曲目"Bunker Bumper"与"Global Bully"为核心，分析其音乐如何塑造角色的情感与叙事重量。前者被描绘为解构的bossa nova，贝斯鼓标记时间，铜管与弦乐如慢动作旗帜般缠绕，呈现出缺乏和声推进却持续涌动的疲惫感；后者则以仪式感打击乐配合弦乐与铜管的和声汇聚，渲染出革命激情褪去后的哀悼氛围。文章还追溯了这些作品早在2002年《Punch-Drunk Love》时期便被录制的事实，探讨Brion如何将音乐嵌入影像、重塑配乐与画面关系的工作方式。整体属于电影配乐评论范畴，侧重叙事功能与配器分析。

items.body: Love songs have spent a century turning devotion into a virtue simply because somebody found a chorus for it. Modern Friend’s Pictures takes that old bargain and puts a collar around its neck. Writing from the perspective of a dog, Voytek Korab considers the peculiar compromises of modern relationships, where being wanted can mean learning to live entirely on somebody else’s terms. The affection may be real, but the conditions deserve a closer look: be available, be agreeable, and please do not need anything inconvenient. A founding member of My Favorite Robot, Korab has spent years inside underground electronic music, playing everywhere from Coachella and DC-10 to the Rex Club and Montreal’s Piknic Elektronik. Modern Friend grew from a different urge, one he had been carrying for much of the last decade: get back to singing, get back to writing songs, and give a more personal voice to the ideas taking shape around the music. Pictures, the third single from the forthcoming debut album Nothing Out Of Something, carries that return into a brisk new-wave frame where melody and discomfort share the same room. The beat moves with tidy motorik efficiency as Korab keeps the vocals languid and dreamy. The hooks settle in quickly, making an inviting setting for a less comfortable question about what people are willing to surrender in exchange for being wanted. “I hope to one day be your best accessory” gives the joke its sharpest point. Here, a prospective partner is already negotiating their own reduction, volunteering to fit whatever space another person has available. You can be a modern man’s best friend, provided you remember that “stay” is an instruction and not a promise. “Just put up pictures when I’m lost” brings a more tender possibility into the song through the familiar image of lost-dog flyers fastened to streetposts. Beneath the joke sits a vulnerable hope: if I go missing, care enough to come looking. Korab describes the feeling beneath the song’s humor: “It’s a song about wanting to be loved for who you are, while quietly realizing that sometimes love can begin to feel more like possession, decoration, or convenience than connection.” That distinction gives Pictures its emotional weight. The pet becomes a metaphor for the partner who learns to accept affection on somebody else’s schedule, gradually editing out the needs and opinions that might spoil the arrangement. Small concessions accumulate until one person’s comfort determines the shape of both their lives. Being needed can feel reassuring enough to postpone asking whether that need leaves room for your independence. Korab keeps the premise playful, but the imbalance is familiar: one person waits faithfully for attention while the other decides when to give it. Watch the video for Pictures below: Mixed by Justin Drake at Bakehouse Studios in London and mastered by Ali X in Mexico, Pictures gives its uneasy observations an appealing pop finish. Its easy movement suits the satire: the song makes accommodation sound pleasant enough that you can understand how somebody might overlook the cost. By the end, Pictures has made its canine perspective uncomfortably familiar. Modern romance is for the dogs when loyalty becomes an expectation and affection remains a reward. Even the most faithful companion deserves more than an occasional scrap of attention. Listen to Pictures below and order the single via Permaculture here. items._cn_summary: Modern Friend 的单曲《Pictures》以宠物的视角切入现代亲密关系的命题：当渴望被爱逐渐滑向被拥有、被装饰、被便利化的状态，伴侣关系如何退化为服从与等待。歌词通过走失犬启事的意象，在幽默外壳下包裹对独立性的不安追问。Korab 将来自地下电子场景的多年经验带入新浪潮框架，节拍带有德式摩托式推进，旋律流畅易记但承载不安的语义张力。整体制作在伦敦与墨西哥两地完成混音与母带处理，声音干净克制，为讽刺性的歌词提供了恰如其分的流行外壳。作品在主题层面有清晰的概念深度，但在声音设计与实验性上偏向温和，对追求前沿声响的听众而言冲击力有限。

items.body: Gary Numan released his sixteenth solo studio album, “Dead Son Rising”, on 15 September 2011 through Mortal Records. The album turns 15 this year. Numan co-wrote and co-produced the record with Ade Fenton, his collaborator on the 2006 album “Jagged”, and recorded it in London. “Dead Son Rising” grew out of demos left over from earlier sessions. Numan described the source material as barely recognizable by the time the album took shape: “The original ideas that sparked off these songs are now barely visible. It’s grown into another animal, something more experimental.” What is on Gary Numan’s ‘Dead Son Rising’ The album runs 11 tracks and 52:50: “Resurrection”, “Big Noise Transmission”, “Dead Sun Rising”, “When the Sky Bleeds, He Will Come”, “For the Rest of My Life”, “Not the Love We Dream Of”, “The Fall”, “We Are the Lost”, “For the Rest of My Life (Reprise)”, “Into Battle” and “Not the Love We Dream Of (Piano Version)”. A digital-only bonus track, “Dead Sun Rising (Early Version)”, also appeared. “Resurrection” and “Into Battle” are instrumentals, described by Numan and Fenton as soundtrack-style material. Several songs reworked earlier, unreleased material. “Dead Sun Rising” rebuilt “What Have I Become” from the 2006 “Jagged” sessions. “For the Rest of My Life” and “The Fall” both trace back to the 2000 album “Pure”, reworking the tracks “Always” and “Look” respectively; both had circulated in earlier mixes on Numan’s live “Purified” tour audio programme. “We Are the Lost” reworked “Mercy” from the “Jagged” sessions. “We Are the Lost” and “Dead Sun Rising” also carry elements of a science-fiction story Numan had been writing over the preceding years. Numan sang and played keyboards. Fenton produced, played keyboards and piano, and handled programming. Tim Muddiman played guitar and bass, Steve Harris played guitar, and Nathan Boddy played keyboard. The label issued the album across three formats: a standard CD, a CD/DVD/vinyl edition with “The Fall” promo video, behind-the-scenes footage, an exclusive interview and a gallery, and a limited numbered box set with a 48-page art book, a signed print, a gatefold vinyl pressing and an exclusive 12-inch of remixes of “The Fall” by Motor and South Central. “The Fall” served as lead single, previewed in a promo edit on Numan’s official site on 28 August 2011. “Dead Sun Rising” had already surfaced as a radio edit via The Quietus on 12 August 2011, ahead of the album. “Dead Son Rising” entered the UK Albums Chart at number 87 for a single week and reached number 5 on the German alternative albums chart. About Gary Numan Gary Numan was born Gary Anthony James Webb in Hammersmith, London, in 1958. He formed Tubeway Army in 1977 and switched from guitar to synthesizer after finding a Minimoog left behind in a studio during the sessions for the band’s 1978 self-titled debut. Tubeway Army’s second album, “Replicas”, topped the UK chart in 1979 behind the single “Are ‘Friends’ Electric?”, also a UK number 1. Numan then dropped the group name and released “The Pleasure Principle” later that year, a second consecutive UK chart-topper, followed by “Telekon” in 1980, a third. His commercial standing in Britain declined through the mid-to-late 1980s even as the catalogue’s influence spread through electronic and industrial music. Numan began working with producer Ade Fenton on the 2006 album “Jagged”, a partnership that continued into “Dead Son Rising” in 2011 and has run through most of his output since. Numan and Fenton followed “Dead Son Rising” with “Splinter (Songs From A Broken Mind)” in 2013, covered here in Gary Numan announces new ‘Splinter (Songs From A Broken Mind)’ album and tour – listen to first track!, and “Savage (Songs from a Broken World)” in 2017, reported in Gary Numan to release new ‘Savage (Songs from a Broken World)’ album on double vinyl (with 2 bonus tracks). He discussed his studio approach in Gary Numan – ‘After doing this for over 35 years I still get excited about what’s around the corner’ – Tech-Talk with DJ Wildhoney. Numan has also worked outside his solo catalogue during this period, collaborating with John Foxx on the release covered in John Foxx and Gary Numan collaborate on ’21st Century: a Man, a Woman and a City’ album – out in 2 physical versions, joining Jean-Michel Jarre’s “Electronica” project, and touring North America in 2023 in direct support of Ministry, as reported in Ministry announces 2023 headline tour dates with direct support from Gary Numan & Front Line Assembly. Fifteen years on, “Dead Son Rising” marks the album where the Numan-Fenton partnership moved past its “Jagged” starting point into the denser, soundtrack-inflected sound that carried through “Splinter” and “Savage”.
items._cn_summary: 这是Gary Numan第十五周年纪念的第十六张个人专辑《Dead Son Rising》，由Mortal Records发行。专辑由Numan与长期合作者Ade Fenton共同创作制作，录制于伦敦。素材源自早期未发表的创作积累，Numan自述原始动机在成型过程中已变得模糊，呈现出更具实验性的面貌。全碟收录11首曲目，时长52分50秒，结构包括电影配乐式器乐曲、重新演绎的旧作以及与科幻叙事相关的概念化创作。制作团队以键盘、钢琴与编程为核心，搭配吉他与贝斯。多版本发行包含数字版、CD/DVD/黑胶套装及限量编号礼盒。歌曲《The Fall》担任首发单曲。从音乐风格看，该专辑属于工业电子与暗潮的交集，融合了合成器音色、程式化节奏与偏冷的氛围铺陈，符合Numan一贯的电子化人声处理与极简主义结构。

items.body: Soft Vein All We’ve Known of Heaven Artoffact Records If you’ve been following Los Angeles’ Soft Vein since their first LP in 2023 but hadn’t heard any of the pre-release singles for new album All We’ve Known of Heaven you might be forgiven for wondering if it’s even the same project. It’s not that Justin Chamberlain has entirely changed his approach to music: you’re still getting a lot of the same melancholic melodies of the project’s debut and sophomore records, but with the hyper-gloomy and often dour mood of those albums replaced with a powerful, hopeful yearning. Coupled with Chamberlain’s rapid growth as a songwriter, All We’ve Known of Heaven has emerged as one of year’s most moving and engaging listens. Chamberlain’s biggest asset in both his songcraft and his performances is his sense of restraint. The album’s feeling of intimacy comes directly from how simultaneously laidback and vulnerable it comes across; a cut like “Forgetting You” works because its clean, Knopfler-esque guitar and multi-tracked vocals bring you in, setting you up for the big drum machine claps and a damnably catchy chorus. The effect is that it feels like the songs being sung to you as a listener, not at you. When Chamberlain asks “Is this all we are?/All we know?” on the jaw-dropping synthpop gem “All We’ve Known of Heaven” it’s a question directed at the world at large, its ruminations on the sad state of things in the early days of the 21st century building to a plea for a kinder, more loving world. It’s stirring by virtue of the honesty with which it’s delivered, both vocally and musically, from its tasteful synthwork and the smooth closing saxophone solo, to the cathartic introspection of its lyrics and Chamberlain’s deeply heartfelt vocals. The warmth and passion of the songs are fully supported by the wonderfully lush and refined production from Chamberlain himself, assisted by live member Andrea Mantione of Nuovo Testamento. “Learning to Talk” is a sweet love song about the sense of discovery in being with another person, its little synth and guitar trills and half-whispered opening verse building momentum gradually, the space around the instruments growing into a powerful climax. In one of the record’s best moments on “Chekhov”, the edge of bitterness and disappointment in Chamberlain’s voice is perfectly matched by the ghostly pads that hang behind him like a reminder, suggesting a soft but everpresent ache. Similarly, the Cocteau Twins guitars that adorn “White Towers (White Shores)” work so well because the song’s programmed drums and keys are locked in beneath them, lifting the song up while also pushing it forwards. All We’ve Known of Heaven is comforting, quietly confident, unhurried, and above all an incredibly lovely record to just sit and listen to. Justin Chamberlain’s willingness to let the songs speak for themselves is certainly a part of it; while no doubt there’s passion and investment in every moment of the LP, it’s all presented with an unpretentious and open candor that makes it easy to get swept up in its grand swells of emotion. An absolute stunner of a album, and one of the year’s best to date. Recommended. Buy it. items._cn_summary: Soft Vein的第二张专辑展现出一种温暖的转变，从此前阴郁忧郁的基调转向充满希望的渴求情绪。Chamberlain在词曲创作和演唱上展现出成熟的克制力，作品通过简洁的吉他编排与分层人声营造亲密感，在鼓机节奏与抓耳副歌之间形成层次。制作精良而丰满，加入了萨克斯独奏与Cocteau Twins式的吉他质感。专辑探讨了当代世界的精神状态，歌词直指对更温柔世界的渴望，情感表达真挚而内省。从音乐元素看，制作中融入了synthpop与dream pop的特征，与暗潮听众的口味有部分交集，但整体仍偏向主流独立电子流行领域，缺乏显著的实验性突破或激进的声音设计。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.excerpt:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds
items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手兼音乐档案学家Dominique Cravic与地下漫画家Robert Crumb共同发起的Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，是其第五张作品。乐队以bal-musette风格为核心，广泛融合拉格泰姆、jug乐队、法国香颂、skiffle等被遗忘的早期音乐类型。演奏使用了手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等大量非常规乐器。27首短曲中Cravic以类似Maurice Chevalier的念白式唱法演绎，其中幽默的《Ukulele Lady》翻唱自1925年原作，向已故法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的《N'oublie pas Gréco》以及《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典改编也包含在内。整体呈现出对老式78转唱片时代音乐的发掘与再活化，乐手虽年逾七十仍以严肃态度呈现。

On serait tent� de mettre Alphataurus dans le m�me panier dor�, avec son superbe premier album �ponyme, � condition de ne pas tenir compte de son deuxi�me, enregistr� la m�me ann�e mais paru seulement en 1992 suite � la dissolution de son auteur, ni de AttosecondO, celui de 2012, excellent mais pas aussi indispensable que son illustre pr�d�cesseur.Plus de 50 ans apr�s cette annus mirabilis, Alphataurus est de retour, port� par deux membres historiques, le clavi�riste Pietro Pellegrini et le guitariste Guido Wassermann (malheureusement disparu apr�s la fin de l'enregistrement). Oui, mais en partie seulement car 2084: Viaggio nel Nulla, fiction dystopique au th�mes philosophiques et existentiels, alterne des titres de RPI qui ont encore le feu sacr� (une bonne moiti� du disque) avec une sorte de prog classieux mais passe-partout qui semble avancer avec nonchalance sur des accords bluesy (� Pista 6 � bizzarement plac�e en d�but d'album, et sauv� par un pont magique au mellotron), se rapprochant malencontreusement de la vari�t�-rock italienne de luxe (� Viaggio nel nulla �, d�cevant malgr� un d�but prometteur et un th�me m�lodique ent�tant), un peu comme a pu le faire r�cemment PFM dans ses moments les moins inspir�s (d'ailleurs, la voix du chanteur Franco Giaffreda peut �tre compar�e � celle de Franz Di Cioccio). � Flashback (apocalisse) � est plus convaincant avec son rythme clairement syncop� et � contretemps en m�moire de Gentle Giant, ses cassures m�lodiques assum�es, son petit solo de moog fac�tieux, ses clins d'?il jazzy, et son �nergie positive communicative. � Meta e met� � (6:36) boxe dans la m�me cat�gorie voire un cran au-dessus avec un jeu de jambe rythmique impr�visible, des uppercuts solistes pleins de s�ve et une m�lodie d'acier dans un �crin de velours. Tout cela n'est pas d�shonorant et m�me plut�t sympathique, fabriqu� consciencieusement avec les moyens d'aujourd'hui, de fa�on tr�s professionnelle par de vrais amoureux du prog. Une premi�re partie dynamique, toute voile dehors, qui doit beaucoup au Banco de la grande �poque avec ses arp�ges d'orgue Hammond et son piano r�p�titif, une deuxi�me partie plus acoustique, construite comme � Impressioni di Settembre � de PFM, avec un refrain sublime, v�ritable d�fi � tous ceux qui voudront se retenir de chanter � tue-t�te en le reprenant en ch?ur, tout est fait pour faire naitre des feux d'artifice entre nos oreilles, nous en mettre plein la vue et nous cacher le scintillement des �toiles. D'un RPI moderne de bonne facture, qu'on peut r��couter souvent avec plaisir en sifflotant les m�lodies comme si on les avaient toujours entendues, 2084: Viaggio nel Nulla devient avec � Wormhole � une sortie-�v�nement � ne pas manquer, propos�e par un v�t�ran du RPI digne de sa l�gende.

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Over its near-20 years of existence, Utah's Rylee McDonald has seen his high school musical project turn into a kind of family affair, now adding his partner and wife and their two children to the mix. Still, the Rush- and Led Zeppelin-inspired artist has emerged as his own musical force.1. "In A Lone and Dreary World" (19:03) a djenty low end does not deter this prog extravaganza from taking us on a journey that reminds me of the music of 21st Century projects like LIFESIGNS and NUMEN and even COSMOGRAF and DAVE BRONS . . . (if a little metal edge were applied). Though I am not a fan of this kind of "plastic" drum sound, I very much appreciate the skills and creativity of the performance on the batterie exhibited here by Mike Lofgreen (though it is also mixed into the soundscape as a kind of anomaly of isolated individually-distinguished sterility; that is, the rest of the sounds are given those standard effects we now associate automatically with prog, i.e. reverbs, distortions, gates, sustains, compressions, etc.) Oh! really love the voice of Kristen McDonald. The collective sound of the band's vocal palette reminds me of short-lived band from Naughties, THE REASONING as well as second- and third- album PURE REASON REVOLUTION (2009's Amor Vincit Omnia and 2010's Hammer and Anvil). Paired up with those syncopated djenty guitar chords and we have quite a cool sound and mix. Then you have to take into consideration the common human plight being expressed in the song lyrics: dissatisfaction and distrust of all we've been raised to believe and value, all we've been told--including that coming from parents and family--learning to listen to and trust one's own inner voice and inner truths and beliefs--the awakening to the power of a spiritual perspective (perhaps even a Christian rebirth): "No enemies" and "saved and sound." Though the length taken to deliver the message/story is a bit over-protracted, it is effective and well-rendered with little or no fluff and appropriate nuance and theatrics. Nice work. (36.5/40) 2. "Faiths Window" (5:20) with industrial horn humming in the background a dirty-distorted electric guitar's two-chord strum repeats itself, occasionally moving between subtly different chords as Rylee McDonald sing/talks over the top, turning into singing as the rest of the band's sound cascades into the mix. It's heavy but it's symphonic with the layers of instruments easy to distinguish from each other. In the fourth minute the lyrics are delivered through growl-screams before the McDonald family choir takes over. A metal instrumental passage takes over with searing electric guitar, etc. but then Kristen emerges as the lead vocalist, taking us to the song's (rather sudden) end. (8.875/10)3. "Patience" (4:53) a normal rock sound palette over which Rylee's single male voice leads the way gradually turns heavy metal with the chorus, playing out as such into the final fadeout of electronic keyboards. A solid song but there is nothing very new or innovative here. (8.75/10)4. "Past Life Parable" (5:03) more solid heavy prog steering toward the more sophisticated hair band sounds and music of the 1970s and 1980s, the big difference here is the use of djenty guitar chords and some more-modern sounds as well as an admirable level of sophistication in the construct/composition. (8.875/10)5. "Gravity I" (2:35) nice Spanish acoustic guitar play surrounded by proggy drum 'n' bass and textural synth washes and other keyboard and, eventually, electric guitar effects. Impressive drum play toward the end--just before the transition/bridge to "Gravity II." (4.625/5) 6. "Gravity II" (4:49) bleeding over from the previous "introductory" song, Rylee's voice in the lead position is backed/doubled by Kristen. Nice use of organ bass pedals and harpsichord sound in the third minute, but then we are quickly back into the metal, even djenty music long before the minute's end. I really like the guitar djent-play in this section (as well as the more subdued vocal performance), but then we shift back into hyperdrive with the machine gun bass pedal play for a few bars before cutting out for a near-a cappella passage, but then we nearly as quickly and suddenly find ourselves back in the fray of machine gun beats and rapid-fire beat-down low end guitar chords. Still, I like and respect it overall. (9/10)7. "Animals" (5:34) Rylee's single male voice is singing while only accompanied by lone acoustic guitar picking. After one time through a round of the verse and chorus the keys, bass pedals, and stark drum play join in the now split (R & L) two-acoustic guitar picking foundation. I wish I could pick out who Rylee's voice reminds me of: it's definitely one of STYX's lead vocalists: either Tommy Shaw or Dennis DeYoung. The McDonald family choir is cited for this song but their role is, sadly, rather quiet, minor. Still, this is a pretty cool song--one that only lacks for seriously brainworm melodies. (9.125/10) Total Time 47:17The McDonald family's sound and style cannot help but be compared to the bands mentioned above--especially THE REASONING and early PURE REASON REVOLUTION but also bands like RUSH, STYX, INTROITUS and MEER. From its Led Zeppelin inspiration and Rush fueling and modeling, the band seems to have come into its own: into something that sounds like . . . but is really their own thing--which is really nice.A-/five stars; though this kind of Classic Rock and sophisticated 80s Metal blend of prog is not really among my high preferences, I do appreciate the creative and complex song structures built here as well as the wonderful vocal work rendered by the collective members of the McDonald family (really, Rylee and Kristen).
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自犹他州家族乐队的重型前卫金属专辑，以Rush和Led Zeppelin为灵感来源，将djent风格低音与管弦乐层次相结合。专辑包含一首近20分钟的长篇作品，融合了电子键盘、失真吉他与人声合唱，歌词探讨信仰觉醒与内在真理等主题。评论者对女主唱Kristen的声音赞誉有加，称其音色令人联想到Pure Reason Revolution等乐队。尽管制作精良、技巧扎实，且具有一定的叙事性，但整体仍属于传统前卫金属范畴，在实验性、电子融合或即兴探索方面鲜有突破，与用户偏好的实验前卫、自由爵士、IDM电子及暗潮工业等方向距离较远。

items.body: Review by Neuroprog — Octobre is one of the first progressive rock albums from Quebec, released in 1973. The wonderful compositions on this album allow Pierre Flynn to showcase his full talent. He is truly one of Quebec's finest singers, a real hidden gem. Overall, the songs are built around powerful and catchy riffs. This is therefore not the most progressive album out there: it does not particularly seek to push musical boundaries or necessarily build toward epic moments. It is instead one of the great Quebec rock albums, with clear influences from the progressive rock movement of the time. It was only after this album that the band would go on to develop and complicate its compositions further. It is unfortunate that this excellent album and band are not nearly as well known as Harmonium, Robert Charlebois, Beau Dommage, Offenbach, Paul Pich�, and others.More specifically, the album features a lot of changes in rhythm despite containing only eight tracks and running for less than 30 minutes. We go from songs like Si on partait, a more straightforward rock song with a frantic pace, to much more nuanced and slower pieces featuring melancholic lyrics sung beautifully by Pierre Flynn. Flynn also shines on several tracks with his expressive organ and piano solos.To fully appreciate this album, it is essential to understand French, and especially "joual", as well as the Quebec specific references of the period. Dans ma ville is a perfect example of a song built around two completely different tempos. You can feel the musical crescendo throughout the verses before everything comes back down for a gentle chorus, conveying the feelings of anger and nostalgia that run through the song. This combination of emotion and rhythm is present throughout the album, reinforcing the power of Flynn's vocals.The closing track, La maudite machine, is an anthem in which the importance of the lyrics takes precedence over the melody. Strangely enough, it is the best-known song on the album, although it is not necessarily the most musically interesting one.4/5
items._cn_summary: 这张1973年的魁北克前卫摇滚专辑共收录八首曲目，时长不足三十分钟。乐评指出作品以朗朗上口的强劲riff为骨架，并不刻意追求音乐边界的突破，也缺少史诗化的展开段落，因此更接近带有前卫摇滚色彩的摇滚专辑，而非典型的前卫摇滚。Pierre Flynn的演唱、键盘与管风琴演奏是亮点，歌曲在节奏和情绪上存在明显反差，从快节奏的摇滚段落过渡到带有忧郁歌词的慢板。终曲以歌词为重，旋律相对次要。整体上，乐评肯定其作为魁北克摇滚代表作的历史地位，但承认其知名度远不及同期的Harmonium、Beau Dommage等。
